attribution.note: Zitron's own gloss on a Goldman passage he quotes. The summary and the no-gains assertion are his words.

semantics.note: Faithful on the main points. It drops the minor clause about layoff justification. The speaker's 'cost of their employees' is broader than the engineering-only figure in the source.

contract.note: Using the engineering-headcount denominator matches the source he cites and is fair. Requiring evidence that gains were absent at the same company is reasonable, and silence about gains rightly does not count.

evidence.note: The Goldman report dated Apr 15 2026 gives one datapoint: engineering inference costs approaching about 10% of headcount cost. This supports only the spending part. It does not name the company, says nothing about operational gains, and is a single datapoint, not 'some companies'.

reviews.rationale: Goldman's anecdote partly supports the spending figure: one unnamed datapoint, engineering only, 'approaching' 10%. Nothing in the packet shows whether that company saw stability, quality or efficiency gains, and the contract needs both parts. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own explanatory assertion in his post.

semantics.note: Captures the firm core claim of 'vast majority' and 'currently'. It omits the clause about metering by requests or rate limits, which is descriptive.

contract.note: Reading 'subsidize' as below actual serving cost fits his own gloss that companies lose money unless usage is low. The plain reading is ordinary, and counting by service is a reasonable choice.

evidence.note: Bessemer, Feb 2026: AI businesses see 50-60% gross margins. This covers broad AI businesses, not subscription-only economics, and predates April 2026. It cannot measure how many subscription services are subsidized.

reviews.rationale: No representative sample matches subscription revenue to serving costs for April 2026. The only item is broad, earlier gross-margin context, which neither supports nor refutes the claim that most subscription services are subsidized.

attribution.note: Zitron's own allegation, which he introduces as coming out and saying it. The Stevenson material he quotes is someone else's.

semantics.note: The draft drops 'I think'. That is not one of the policy's hedges, and with 'come out and say it' the claim reads as a firm allegation. The scope of 'the AI startups' is undefined.

contract.note: The standard of material misrepresentation is fair. The Q1 2026 window and the choice of named companies are the evaluator's, not the speaker's, so the interpretation shapes the result.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own disclosure labels its $14B as run-rate revenue. This weighs against a realized-revenue misreading but does not validate the number.
TechCrunch, Apr 2026: $6B is Cursor's year-end run-rate forecast, not current revenue. It falls outside the target quarter.
Fast Company reports a founder's allegation that some startups present contracted ARR (CARR) as ARR. No companies are named and no records are reconciled.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no matched representations and records showing material overstatement by named startups or a representative group. It also has no complete reconciliation that clears them. Anthropic's labeled run rate and Cursor's forecast are context, and the CARR allegation is unverified.

attribution.note: Zitron's own summary of his calculation.

semantics.note: The minimums and the 15.2GW cohort are kept. The draft drops 'reserved' and 'through partners', which is a minor narrowing.

contract.note: Requiring both allocations to sit inside the same under-construction cohort, without double-counting, is a fair reading of the summary.

evidence.note: Epoch, Apr 17 2026: Stargate sites are under active construction, with about 9GW projected by 2029. Phase-level capacity under construction and membership in the Sightline cohort are not given.
Anthropic disclosure, Nov 2025: up to 1GW with Microsoft/NVIDIA. This is a maximum commitment, not a site under construction. It does not refute the claim without the cohort data.
Anthropic/Amazon, Apr 20 2026: up to 5GW, with nearly 1GW online by end of 2026. It is not mapped to construction phases in the cohort.

reviews.rationale: The Sightline 15.2GW inventory is unavailable. The packet confirms large OpenAI construction and several Anthropic capacity agreements, but none of it allocates capacity under construction within that cohort. Neither the 4.6GW nor the 4GW minimum can be confirmed or refuted.
